newsitem.title: UK: Israeli psychic Geller offers Kashmir mediation.
newsitem.headline: Israeli psychic Geller offers Kashmir mediation.

text.p: Israeli psychic Uri Geller has put up a $50,000 reward for the release of Western hostages held in Kashmir for almost two years and offered to act as an intermediary with the guerrillas who seized them.
He also urged millions of people around the world to concentrate their minds every day and try to reach the kidnappers.
"The families approached me and asked me if I could help. Obviously I agreed as what you are talking about here is human life," he told Reuters on Thursday.
"I think they had come to a dead end. They had exhausted all their avenues. They believe in mind power," he added.
Britons Paul Wells and Keith Mangan were abducted by the shadowy Al-Faran guerrilla group while trekking through the Himalayas in July 1995.
German Dirk Hasert, Norwegian Hans Christian Ostroe and Americans Donald Hutchings and John Childs were also captured.
Childs escaped and Ostroe was beheaded. There has been no trace of the other four for several months, raising doubts over whether they are still alive.
Geller, best known for his ability apparently to bend spoons by willpower alone, said an open letter has been put in Indian newspapers with a message to the group.

"We are willing to listen to them and hear their side on condition they give a sign the hostages are alive. I would be very willing to take their message to any leader they wanted to. I am prepared to pay $50,000 as a reward for their release."
Geller said he had won the backing of British Foreign Secretary Malcolm Rifkind for his intermediary offer.
The families of the Britons distributed leaflets on Monday in the Himalayan region appealing for help in finding their loved ones.
As well as offering to act as go-between, Geller also made another more unconventional approach in his bid to secure the hostages' release.
"I am asking people to concentrate every day at 11 o'clock and try to reach the kidnappers and make mind contact to try and influence them," he said.
Geller said he had devoted a special corner on his website to the hostages - http://www.urigeller.com.
He agreed his intervention was unusual: "Remember I am from Israel and they are Moslems. But that is why I think they are going to respond."
